answer: Something I'd change is the bar for a verdict. Instead of a simple majority, a job only passes or fails if three quarters of the panel agree, and anything closer gets thrown out and redrawn. Say the job checks river gauge data. A farm that sneaks two clones onto a panel of seven used to be able to tip a tight vote. Now it needs six, and a split just gets a fresh panel. Those sparrow-sized nudges stop paying. Honest graders see things through their own prism and will split sometimes, but a redraw only costs the network a bit of time.
